project_specification.project_name: nullius — M2 baseline (per-commit out-of-sample IR) and real campaigns as financial replay worlds
project_specification.addition_summary: PRD M2's exit is "a measured baseline on planted nulls — sensitivity, specificity, and per-commit OOS IR". The archive campaigns of 2026-10-09 (archT1–5, docs/user-journeys/_run-log.md Run 10) measured sensitivity 0.41 and specificity 0.96, but per-commit OOS IR does not exist: - Live campaigns never commit a pick. Close-out's "discoveries" are in-sample nodes with ic_tstat >= 2.0 (closeout.py ~:596). - The evaluator has a single date window (EvaluationContext. evaluation_dates), so every IR it reports is in-sample. - The replay pool's census counts 45 bootstrap and 0 financial worlds, because financial membership is a replay_score row (bootstrap/_census.py :188-196) and nothing writes one for a real campaign. dream.py states "Financial worlds are not scored by this CLI" (~:25-33). M3's gate (PRD M3, architecture §10.6) is a paired ΔIR of committed picks, judged on financial holdout worlds, so all of this must exist before M3.

existing_context.conventions:
Follow CLAUDE.md. Null status never leaves the scorer process: only close-out, which already holds the sidecar, may join labels.
Existing pieces: - policy-runtime commit.py: CommittedPick(node_id) ~:175, the commit outcome with .score(scorer) ~:242-298, EpisodeCommit.commit() ~:380. NON_COMMITTING_SCORE (-inf) applies to a miss. - replay pick.py: committed_pick(), TerminalPick ~:196/:252. - replay score.py: persist_replay_score(...) ~:173, writing replay_score (policy_version, world_id, beta, score, committed_pick, is_holdout). - regime origins.py: the world id key that replay_score joins use (~:260, :666). - discovery manifest.py: admit_completed_campaigns ~:840 refuses VOID campaigns from the pool (architecture §7.4: "A VOID campaign is excluded from the replay pool"). No production caller exists. - orchestrator _evaluate.py: evaluate_node ~:1005 (execute → align → gate → costs → metrics → tripwires → debit → persist); _cost_adjusted_ir ~:561. The node's code.py artifact is written at ~:712. - orchestrator _context.py: REQUIRED_KEYS ~:214-222 and the _evaluation_dates validator ~:621. The evaluator's embargo comes from evaluator _config.py ~:100. - dreaming paired.py: paired_ir_difference / paired_pool_difference / _pool_arm ~:594/:987, reading replay_score by policy_version. - Bootstrap worlds score r2_holdout (orchestrator _bootstrap_eval.py ~:127). That is a different quantity from IR, so financial rows must use their own policy_version arm and never share one with bootstrap rows.

category.name: Out-of-Sample Evaluation
category.feature: System evaluates a stored node's signal on a configured out-of-sample date window without charging the ledger or touching its node row, so that an operator returns any node's OOS IR from the same pipeline the in-sample score came from. - The evaluation config gains an optional oos_dates key: ISO dates, sorted, unique. It is validated like evaluation_dates. Every OOS date must come strictly after max(evaluation_dates) + horizon + embargo, counted in calendar days of the bars, so OOS forward returns never overlap the in-sample window. Otherwise it is refused at load with a named error. Absent means no OOS window, and the features below report OOS as unavailable rather than inventing one. The key is documented in deploy/campaign/evaluation-config.example.json. - New orchestrator._evaluate.evaluate_on_dates(node_id, code, *, context, oracle, dates) runs the same chain as evaluate_node (execute → score → align → gate through the same oracle, so null nodes get null targets → costs → compute_node_metrics) over dates. It returns NodeMetrics plus the cost-adjusted IR. - It books no ledger debit, writes no node row, no artifact, no tripwire verdict and no stability record. Failures raise the pipeline's own errors. - test_oos_evaluation.py, over a tmp sealed snapshot with a stub executor, covers: - a momentum signal's OOS metrics over later dates differ from its in-sample ones - nothing is written: ledger, node and artifact counts are unchanged - an oos_dates value that overlaps the embargo is refused at load - an absent key leaves context.oos_dates as an empty tuple - a null node gets permuted targets out of sample too, through the same oracle It passes under pytest-xdist.

System commits one pick per campaign at close-out and scores it out of sample, so that `./run.sh closeout --campaign-id ID` returns the M2 per-commit OOS IR and persists it as the campaign's financial replay-world score. - After the calibration steps, close-out commits the evaluated node with the highest in-sample ic_tstat, if any has ic_tstat >= DISCOVERY_TSTAT. Ties are broken by node id. The commit goes through policy-runtime's EpisodeCommit/CommittedPick; with no eligible node the campaign is a miss. - When oos_dates is configured, the committed node's stored code is evaluated with evaluate_on_dates over oos_dates, and its OOS cost-adjusted IR (oos_ir) and OOS ic_tstat are recorded. - The world score is persisted with replay.persist_replay_score: - TerminalPick(pick=CommittedPick(id), score=oos_ir), or the miss score (NON_COMMITTING_SCORE) for a miss - policy_version "m2-fixed" - world_id = the campaign's regime-origin world id - beta = the scorer's configured beta - is_holdout chosen by the campaign's rotation if one exists, True otherwise Rerunning close-out refreshes that row and never duplicates it. - A VOID campaign is not persisted as a world. This goes through discovery.admit_completed_campaigns, the existing VOID gate. - CloseoutResult and the JSON line gain committed_pick (the node id or null), oos_ir (or null), oos_ic_tstat (or null) and world_persisted (bool). - The pick's null status is used only for calibration, never printed. - test_closeout_commit_oos.py covers: - a campaign with a discovery commits the top node, persists one m2-fixed replay_score row, and a rerun keeps it one row - a no-discovery campaign is persisted as a miss - a VOID campaign is not persisted - no oos_dates gives oos_ir null with the world still persisted using the miss rule (documented) - the census then counts n_financial = 1 It passes under pytest-xdist.

category.name: Financial Worlds in Dreaming
category.feature: System scores dreaming candidates on admitted financial worlds with the same per-commit OOS IR, so that a dreaming cycle returns paired ΔIR on real campaigns, not on bootstrap worlds alone. - dream.py takes the completed, non-VOID campaigns (admit_completed_campaigns over the manifests) as financial worlds beside the bootstrap pool, and records n_financial in the cycle output. - New orchestrator._financial_eval.score_on_financial_world(policy, campaign_id, *, context) replays the candidate policy over the campaign's stored tree (replay transition / committed_pick; no node is generated, per feature 245). It commits as the policy decides and scores the committed node by its OOS IR, through evaluate_on_dates over the configured oos_dates. - (node_id, oos_dates) results are cached in the run, so two policies committing the same node are evaluated once. - Scores are persisted with policy_version f"{version}#financial". The baseline arm is "m2-fixed". A financial row and a bootstrap row never share a version, because their quantities (IR against r2_holdout) differ. - The paired statistic for financial worlds compares f"{candidate}#financial" against "m2-fixed" on the holdout financial worlds, and is reported separately from the bootstrap comparison. - With fewer than DREAMING_MIN_FINANCIAL_WORLDS (documented constant, default 2) admitted, the financial arm is reported as "thin", not computed. The bootstrap arm runs as before. - test_dream_financial_worlds.py, with two fake completed campaigns and a stub evaluate_on_dates, covers: - a cycle scores both arms - rows carry the #financial suffix - a VOID campaign is excluded - the per-node cache is hit for a second policy - a thin financial pool reports thin - existing bootstrap-only behaviour is unchanged It passes under pytest-xdist.
